spec.description: Network performance of the embedded monitor (Raspberry Pi 5) connected over Wi-Fi (MERCUSYS_ECD5_5G) to a Mercusys MB135-4G router with a Vodacom LTE backhaul. Ping every 10 s (TCP check when ping fails), router LTE traffic over SNMP every 10 s, Wi-Fi every 2 s, Pi health every 10 s, traceroute and iperf3 on a schedule. Data: VictoriaMetrics on the Pi; vmagent forwards a copy to the laptop receiver (Store-and-forward tab). EEE4022S, UCT.

spec.title: Latency (RTT)
spec.description: round-trip time to 8.8.8.8 from 5 pings every 10 s: avg = average, min = fastest reply, max = slowest reply. a high max with a normal avg means one slow reply.

spec.title: Ping time now
spec.description: The round-trip time to 8.8.8.8, average of 5 pings, every 10 s. lower is better.

spec.title: Packet loss now
spec.description: The 5 pings to 8.8.8.8 that got no reply in the latest check (steps of 20 %). 0 % is normal.

spec.title: Download use now
spec.description: Share of the 10 Mbit/s iNethi reference download link in use now, from the Mercusys router's LTE interface (lte0) over SNMP every 10 s. Yellow from 50 %, red from 70 %. It can go above 100 % if the LTE link is faster than the reference.

spec.title: Upload use now
spec.description: Share of the 5 Mbit/s iNethi reference upload link in use now, from the Mercusys router's LTE interface (lte0) over SNMP every 10 s. Yellow from 50 %, red from 70 %. It can go above 100 % if the LTE link is faster than the reference.

spec.title: Backhaul up (time range)
spec.description: The checks in the chosen time range where the internet link was up. local link down and unknown count as not up. times when the monitor was not running are not counted.

spec.title: Backhaul state over time
spec.description: History of the internet link (backhaul): green = up, red = down, orange = the pi’s own wi-fi was off, grey = not checked yet.

spec.title: Download speed
spec.description: Download on the Mercusys router's LTE interface (lte0), read from the router over SNMP every 10 s. Dashed lines: 5 Mbit/s (yellow, 50 %) and 7 Mbit/s (red, 70 %) of the 10 Mbit/s iNethi reference.

spec.title: Upload speed
spec.description: Upload on the Mercusys router's LTE interface (lte0), read from the router over SNMP every 10 s. Dashed lines: 2.5 Mbit/s (yellow, 50 %) and 3.5 Mbit/s (red, 70 %) of the 5 Mbit/s iNethi reference.

spec.title: Link full (1 minute)
spec.description: Red = the router's LTE link was full for at least 1 whole minute (≥ 70 % of the iNethi reference: 7 Mbit/s down, 3.5 Mbit/s up). Short bursts are not shown. The monitor's own iperf3 tests go to the laptop on the same Mercusys LAN, so they do not use the LTE link and do not cause these blocks.

spec.title: iperf3 test traffic on the link
spec.description:
Shows when the monitor's own iperf3 throughput test was running. Each set is
three tests (TCP upload, TCP download, UDP), about 10 s each, run once in each
of four daily time slots, with a retry an hour later if a set fails. The test
server is reached over Tailscale through the LTE backhaul, so while a test runs
its traffic is included in the router's traffic counters above.

spec.title: Packet loss
spec.description: Percentage of 5 ICMP packets to $target that got no reply, per measurement (steps of 20 %).

spec.title: TCP speed (iperf3)
spec.description: Highest speed during the monitor's iperf3 test to the laptop on the same Mercusys LAN (10 s each way), up to 4 times a day. The test goes Pi → router → laptop over Wi-Fi, so it measures the local network, not the LTE backhaul.

spec.title: UDP jitter
spec.description: How much the delay between packets varied during the 10 s udp test at 500 kbit/s (measured by the server). lower is better.

spec.title: UDP loss
spec.description: The udp packets that did not arrive during the 10 s test (505 packets). 0 % is normal.

spec.title: Latest iperf3 set
spec.description: Results of the newest speed test set (last 24 h): one row per test. udp has no retransmits; tcp has no jitter or loss, so those cells are empty.

spec.title: Latency variation (mdev)
spec.description: How much the 5 ping reply times differed in each check (every 10 s). near 0 = steady link; high = unsteady (jitter). use with the netem jitter test.

spec.title: TCP check
spec.description: Runs only when ping gets no reply: a tcp connection to 1.1.1.1:443 (another company than the ping target). green = the link works, ping was only blocked. red = the link really failed. empty = ping was fine, no check needed.

spec.title: Traceroute result
spec.description: Shows if the path to 8.8.8.8 worked and where it broke. runs when the backhaul goes down, every 30 min while down, when it comes back, and once an hour as a normal baseline. “pi cannot reach gateway” = the problem is the pi’s own first hop.

spec.title: last hop that replied
spec.description: Number of the last router on the path to 8.8.8.8 that replied. Normal = the hop number of 8.8.8.8 itself in the hourly baseline traceroute. A lower number during an outage shows where along the path the replies stopped.

spec.title: Latest path (hop by hop)
spec.description: The routers on the way to 8.8.8.8 from the latest traceroute (last hour): hop number, router ip and reply time per probe. hops that did not answer (* * *) are not listed. per-hop times are only a hint: routers answer traceroute at low priority.

spec.title: Wi-Fi signal strength
spec.description: Signal strength the Pi receives from the Mercusys router (MERCUSYS_ECD5_5G), measured every 2 s. Closer to 0 is stronger (e.g. -50 dBm is better than -75 dBm). A sudden drop or gap can explain loss or a local link down.

spec.title: Wi-Fi connected?
spec.description: Is the Pi connected to the Mercusys router's Wi-Fi (MERCUSYS_ECD5_5G)? Checked every 2 s. Red = the Pi's own Wi-Fi was down, so the internet link could not be checked (local link down), not a backhaul failure.

spec.title: Which access point (BSSID)
spec.description: Which access point (BSSID) the Pi was connected to. On the Mercusys router this should be one row (08:8a:f1:cc:ec:d5). A new row means the Pi joined a different access point; a drop at the same time can explain a local link down.

spec.title: Wi-Fi channel (frequency)
spec.description: Radio frequency the Pi uses to talk to the Mercusys router. A step up or down = the router changed channel; devices can briefly drop when that happens.

spec.title: Wi-Fi link rate
spec.description: The speed the Pi's radio and the Mercusys router agreed to use (from iw), every 2 s. It shows radio quality, not internet speed: the real internet speed is in the Throughput tab.

spec.title: Services
spec.description: Is each program the monitor needs running? Checked with systemctl every 10 s.

spec.title: Power and throttling
spec.description: Flags from the Pi firmware (vcgencmd get_throttled), every 10 s. under_voltage = power supply too weak. freq_capped / throttled = the CPU was slowed down. soft_temp_limit = slowed down because of heat. Red at the same time as bad network results means the Pi, not the network, may be the cause.

spec.title: Temperature
spec.description: CPU temperature, every 10 s. Dashed lines: 80 °C = default thermal limit (yellow), 85 °C = hard throttling on all Raspberry Pi models (red), from Raspberry Pi Ltd's thermal white paper (2026).

spec.title: Frequency
spec.description: CPU speed, every 10 s. All 4 cores share one clock (checked: policy0 = CPUs 0-3). The ondemand governor lowers the speed when idle, so dips are normal unless "Power and throttling" shows red at the same time.

spec.title: Input voltage (5 V supply)
spec.description: Supply voltage measured by the Pi 5's power chip (EXT5V_V), every 10 s. The firmware's under-voltage flag in "Power and throttling" is the warning; no threshold line is drawn here.

spec.title: CPU use and load
spec.description: CPU use = how busy all 4 cores were between two readings (10 s apart), from /proc/stat. Load per core = 1-minute load average divided by 4 cores; above 1 means more work was waiting than the CPU could run. A busy Pi can make network readings late.

spec.title: Memory and SD card used
spec.description: How full the Pi's memory (RAM) and SD card are, every 10 s. A full SD card stops VictoriaMetrics saving new measurements.

spec.title: Pi uptime
spec.description: Time since the Pi last started, every 10 s. It goes back to 0 after a reboot.

spec.title: Reboots (time range)
spec.description: How many times the uptime went back to 0 in the chosen time range, which means the Pi rebooted. Data gaps at those times are caused by the monitor restarting, not by the network.

spec.title: Clock and SD card
spec.description: Clock synced = the Pi's time is corrected over the internet (NTP), so timestamps are right. SD card writable = the SD card can still save data; Linux makes it read-only if it finds errors. Checked every 10 s.

spec.title: Health reading errors
spec.description: Health readings that failed, with the reason (e.g. a command that did not answer). Empty = every reading worked.

spec.title: Backhaul state
spec.description: State of the backhaul as decided by the monitor: Up = ping or TCP check succeeded; Down = both failed for 2 checks in a row; Local link down = the Pi's own Wi-Fi is not connected.

spec.title: Data waiting to be sent
spec.description: Size of vmagent's on-disk buffer. Stays near 0 while the laptop receiver is reachable, grows during an outage, and falls back to 0 once the buffered data has been sent.

spec.title: Sent to remote receiver
spec.description: Rate at which vmagent sends data to the laptop receiver, measured between consecutive 15 s samples. Normally a few hundred B/s; a short spike after an outage shows the buffered backlog being sent.

spec.title: Failed send attempts
spec.description: Number of failed attempts to send data to the receiver in each 5-minute window. Non-zero while the receiver or backhaul is down; vmagent retries automatically.

spec.title: Dropped data
spec.description: Data vmagent has discarded instead of delivering: blocks rejected by the receiver (HTTP 400/409) or samples dropped. Any value above 0 means data was lost.

spec.title: Router SNMP
spec.description: Can the monitor read the router's lte0 counters? From snmp_status, every 10 s.

spec.title: Wi-Fi signal now
spec.description:
Latest signal strength of the monitor's Wi-Fi connection to the router, in
dBm, read from the Wi-Fi driver every 2 s. Values closer to 0 mean a stronger
signal. A weak signal can cause loss and delay on the local link that are not
caused by the backhaul; see the Wi-Fi tab for the history.

spec.title: Data waiting to be sent
spec.description: Size of vmagent's on-disk buffer. Stays near 0 while the laptop receiver is reachable, grows during an outage, and falls back to 0 once the buffered data has been sent.

spec.title: Services
spec.description:
Whether each of the four services on the monitor (netmon, victoria, vmagent
and grafana-server) is running, as reported by systemd. The status is
recorded by netmon, so if netmon itself stops, this panel keeps showing its
last values and no new data appears; a stop of netmon is therefore seen as
missing data rather than as "down".

spec.title: Router SNMP
spec.description:
Whether the router answered the monitor's latest SNMP request, polled every
10 s. The upload and download use panels are calculated from these SNMP
readings, so while this shows "No reply" those values are not being updated.
See the Link use tab for the history.

spec.title: Status timeline
spec.description: Result of each ping check (5 pings to 8.8.8.8 every 10 s). no reply = nothing came back. ping error = ping itself reported a problem, e.g. “network is unreachable” when the pi’s wi-fi is off.

spec.title: Ping Errors
spec.description: Errors table, which shows the error messages.

spec.title: Backhaul now
spec.description: Internet link (backhaul) status

spec.title: Network Monitor
